name: delegate_call_risks
description: Delegatecall to a user-controlled/untrusted target address in Solidity contracts
question: The source file in `source` contains a Solidity function that performs `.delegatecall(...)` on an address parameter or other user-supplied/external variable (not a fixed, owner-set, or whitelisted implementation address), allowing an external caller to make the contract delegatecall into an arbitrary attacker-controlled contract that can overwrite the caller's storage, hijack msg.sender context, or execute arbitrary logic with the calling contract's privileges.
criteria: Function accepts an address parameter (e.g. `target`, `implementation`, `to`) that is passed directly into `.delegatecall(...)`
No check restricting the delegatecall target to an admin-set, immutable, or whitelist-approved address (e.g. missing `approvedImplementations[target]` check)
The delegatecall target originates from calldata, a public/external function argument, or other untrusted user input
Access control modifiers like `onlyOwner`/`onlyAdmin` are absent from the function performing the delegatecall
The delegatecall is not restricted to a fixed, previously verified implementation address set only through a controlled upgrade mechanism
